ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the circuit there is a vertical 4Ω resistor, connecting the upper-left node and the lower-left node; the upper branch has a 6V voltage source, marked with the left end as “+” and the right end as “-”, and the right end is connected to terminal a; from the lower-left node to a there is an obliquely placed 2Ω resistor; the lower branch goes from the lower-left node through a 4V voltage source, marked with the left end as “+” and the right end as “-”, then through a 2Ω resistor to terminal b, and terminal b is open-circuited. Reasoning: According to the specified method, take the lower-left node as 0V. Since terminal b is open-circuited, the current in the lower 2Ω resistor is 0, so the voltage drop across this 2Ω resistor is 0, and the potential at point b equals the potential at the right end of the 4V voltage source. From the polarity of the 4V voltage source, V_lower-left - V_b = 4V, so 0 - V_b = 4, giving V_b = -4V. Form a supernode with the upper-left node containing the 6V voltage source and node a. From the polarity of the 6V voltage source, V_upper-left - V_a = 6. The supernode is connected to the reference node only through the left 4Ω resistor and the oblique 2Ω resistor, so KCL is V_upper-left/4 + V_a/2 = 0. Substituting V_upper-left = V_a + 6 gives (V_a + 6)/4 + V_a/2 = 0, namely 3V_a + 6 = 0, therefore V_a = -2V. Thus U_ab = V_a - V_b = -2 - (-4) = 2V.

method.method_draft: Assign a trial loop current I around the upper triangular loop, for example bottom-left → top-left → a → bottom-left. Write KVL along that direction: the resistor drops are 4I and 2I, and crossing the 6 V source from + to − is a 6 V drop, so 4I + 6 + 2I = 0; this gives the signed loop current. Use the resulting current direction and the diagonal 2 Ω resistor to find V_a relative to the bottom-left node. In the bottom branch, since b is open, the current through the bottom 2 Ω resistor is zero, so terminal b is at the same potential as the right side of the 4 V source; the 4 V source polarity gives V_b relative to the bottom-left node. Finally compute U_ab = V_a − V_b.
